actions.justification: Mandatory first step - patient has critical vitals (hypotension, tachycardia, hypoxia, tachypnea, fever) requiring immediate formal assessment per ATS/IDSA CAP guidelines.
Mandatory - patient has SpO2 84% and RR 32, indicating severe respiratory compromise. Respiratory status assessment is required to guide oxygen therapy and potential intubation decisions.
Mandatory - chest radiography is required per ATS/IDSA guidelines to confirm CAP diagnosis and assess extent of infiltrates.
MANDATORY action per guidelines. CBC is essential for evaluating leukocytosis/leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia in this severe CAP patient with septic shock physiology.

Patient has hypotension (BP 88/52), severe hypoxemia (SpO2 84%), tachypnea (RR 32), and confusion — meeting major criteria for severe CAP requiring ICU admission. Must formally assess ICU criteria per ATS/IDSA guidelines immediately.

Blood cultures must be obtained BEFORE antibiotic administration per guidelines. Patient has severe CAP with septic shock and multiple risk factors (COPD, chronic alcohol use, malnutrition) increasing bacteremia risk. Cultures should not delay antibiotics beyond 1 hour.

Formal CURB-65 scoring is needed to document pneumonia severity (confusion, urea/BUN, RR ≥30, BP <90/60, age). This patient likely scores ≥4-5 (confusion, hypotension, RR 32, fever), confirming severe CAP requiring ICU-level care.
Patient is in septic shock (BP 88/52, MAP 64, HR 118). ATS/IDSA guidelines mandate early IV fluid resuscitation for severe CAP with hemodynamic compromise. Immediate crystalloid bolus is required.

ATS/IDSA guidelines require antibiotics within 1 hour for severe CAP. Beta-lactam plus macrolide combination is first-line empiric therapy for severe CAP. No documented penicillin allergy. Patient has been in the ED 30 minutes — antibiotics must be given now.

ATS/IDSA guidelines recommend Legionella urinary antigen testing for severe CAP requiring ICU-level care. This patient meets severe CAP criteria and Legionella is a key pathogen to identify for targeted therapy.
BMP is essential to assess renal function (AKI risk given hypotension/shock), electrolytes, and glucose in this hemodynamically unstable patient with COPD, alcohol use, and malnutrition.
Procalcitonin provides a baseline inflammatory marker to confirm bacterial infection and guide antibiotic stewardship duration in severe CAP.

Sputum culture is recommended by ATS/IDSA guidelines for severe CAP to identify causative pathogens and guide antibiotic de-escalation. It has not yet been ordered and will help tailor therapy, especially important given this patient's comorbidities (COPD, chronic alcohol use, malnutrition) which predispose to atypical and resistant organisms.

Patient has severe CAP with shock (MAP 64, BP 88/52), respiratory failure (SpO2 84%, RR 32), and confusion — meeting ICU criteria. ATS/IDSA guidelines recommend combination antibiotic therapy for severe CAP. Beta-lactam plus macrolide has already been given; adding a respiratory fluoroquinolone provides broader coverage and is indicated for ICU-level CAP management within the 1-hour antibiotic window.

Patient meets severe CAP criteria with septic shock (MAP 64, BP 88/52) and respiratory failure (SpO2 84%, RR 32). ATS/IDSA guidelines mandate ICU transfer for severe CAP; delays worsen mortality. Treating on ward is explicitly contraindicated.
